input: Set up a tip pool agreement for my small cafe staff

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Tip pooling rules vary significantly depending on whether it covers front-of-house only, back-of-house only, or all staff — this defines who is included and excluded from the pool.

The number of staff, their roles (servers, baristas, cooks, managers), and employment types (full-time, part-time, hourly) directly shapes how the agreement is structured and how shares are calculated.
The format of the agreement matters — whether the user needs a written legal document, an internal policy sheet, or a simple tracking spreadsheet determines what needs to be produced.
Tip pooling is governed by federal (FLSA) and state laws that impose hard legal limits, so the user's location determines what is legally permissible in their agreement.
The distribution method — equal split, hours-worked weighting, point/role-based system — is a core design choice that reflects the owner's priorities and staff culture.
Whether this is being set up from scratch, replacing an existing informal arrangement, or formalising something already in practice changes how much groundwork and staff buy-in is needed.
Knowing whether the user wants something staff simply follow, something legally signed off, or something all staff have actively agreed to determines how much formality and process is required.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a tip pool agreement for cafe staff
gold.taskDescription: Create a formal tip pooling arrangement for a small cafe, covering how tips are collected, distributed, and agreed upon among staff.

questions.title: Which staff roles will be included in the tip pool?
questions.description: Determine whether the pool covers front-of-house staff only (servers, baristas), back-of-house (cooks, dishwashers), or all employees — this defines the pool's scope and legal requirements.

questions.title: How many staff members work at your cafe?
questions.description: Establish the total number of employees and their role types (full-time, part-time, hourly) so the agreement can be appropriately sized and share calculations designed.

questions.title: What country and state or region is your cafe in?
questions.description: Tip pooling is subject to strict federal and local labour laws — knowing the location ensures the agreement stays within legal limits and avoids liability.

questions.title: How do you want tips divided among included staff?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred distribution method — equal split, weighted by hours worked, or a points-based system by role — as this is the core mechanic of the agreement.

questions.title: Is this replacing an existing arrangement or starting fresh?
questions.description: Understanding whether staff currently have an informal tip-sharing practice helps determine how much change management and staff communication is needed.

questions.title: What format does the agreement need to be in?
questions.description: Determine whether the output should be a formal signed legal document, a simple internal policy sheet, a tracking spreadsheet, or a combination of these.

questions.title: What does a successful agreement look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify the bar for completion — whether the user needs staff to simply follow a policy, have everyone formally sign off, or get legal review before implementation.
